whatNextBody: Aletheia helps you choose one wise next step first. Ask first, then switch modes when you want a different lens.
askOneQuestionBody: Start with the decision or pressure you are carrying right now.
askNewQuestionBody: The Companion input and wisdom modes stay close at hand.
notificationPromptBody: Receive one quiet daily wisdom prompt.
syncDevicesBody: Keep decisions and reflections across devices.
startDecisionBody: Track a high-stakes choice over time.
modeShapesCounsel: mode is shaping this counsel around
scriptureStudyModeSubtitle: Explore the meaning, context, and connected scriptures.
shareAnswerPrompt: Share Aletheia with someone who may benefit from this kind of counsel.
sharePrivacyNote: This shares the app link only, not your question or Aletheia's private answer.
formationNote: These are quiet signs of formation, not points to chase. The first milestone usually begins with saving one reflection.
milestoneShareTitle: Know someone making a major decision?
milestoneShareBody: You can invite them to Aletheia without sharing anything private from your account.
welcomeCounsel: Bring a real decision, pressure, or money question. I will answer from the curated wisdom library, with emotional clarity and no financial promises.
trustScriptureBody: Scripture references come from Aletheia's curated wisdom library. If a verse appears, you can tap it to see context and why it matters.
trustBoundaryBody: Aletheia will not promise outcomes, predict markets, claim divine certainty, or replace qualified financial, legal, tax, medical, or pastoral counsel.
trustMemoryBody: Signed-in memory helps continuity across decisions, reflections, counsel, and rules of life. It should make guidance more personal without exposing private details unnecessarily.
trustConnectedDataBody: Future health, finance, or device integrations should be permission-by-permission, off by default, and limited to the exact data the user chooses to connect.

money.label: Money
money.intent: Steward resources with peace and clarity.
money.useWhen: Use for spending, debt, saving, investing, financial anxiety, or comparison.
prompts: How do I build wealth without greed?
What does wisdom say about debt?
How do I stop comparing myself financially?

work.label: Work
work.intent: Discern work, calling, leadership, and sustainable ambition.
work.focus: Career moves, leadership, business, burnout, vocation
work.useWhen: Use for job decisions, business ideas, leadership pressure, burnout, or ambition.
prompts: Should I leave my stable job?
How do I know if ambition is healthy?
Should I start this business now?

purpose.label: Purpose
purpose.intent: Slow down and discern the person this decision forms.
purpose.focus: Identity, direction, anxiety, values, long-term clarity
purpose.useWhen: Use when the real question is identity, direction, peace, timing, or values.
prompts: How do I make a decision when I feel unclear?
What if I am chasing success for the wrong reasons?
How do I find peace about my next step?

generosity.label: Generosity
generosity.intent: Give freely without guilt, pressure, or performance.
generosity.focus: Giving, family support, charity, boundaries, sustainability
generosity.useWhen: Use for giving, tithing, helping family, boundaries, or sustainable generosity.
prompts: How do I give without guilt or pressure?
Should I help family financially again?
How much generosity is sustainable for me?

life.label: Life
life.intent: Apply biblical wisdom to ordinary life, formation, and care with steady, grounded attention.
life.focus: Habits, relationships, family, rest, health, recovery, holiness, loneliness
life.useWhen: Use for everyday life decisions, routines, relationships, habits, rest, conflict, loneliness, addiction, temptation, prayer life, or when the right next step is a quiet act of obedience rather than a major decision.
prompts: How do I stay faithful in a hard season?
What do I do when I feel stuck in an unhealthy pattern?
How do I respond when loneliness or temptation gets heavy?

gratitude3day.title: 3-Day Gratitude Practice
gratitude3day.description: Three days of quiet noticing — one ordinary gift, one steady presence, one area where contentment is growing.

day1.principle: Give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
day1.prompt: Notice one ordinary gift today that you might normally overlook. Write a brief note about it.
day1.practice: Name one ordinary mercy you almost missed.

day2.principle: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; his steadfast love endures forever.
day2.prompt: Think about someone whose steadfast presence has shaped your discernment. Write what you are grateful for about them.
day2.practice: Name a person whose steady presence you are grateful for.

day3.principle: I have learned, in whatever state I am, to be content.
day3.prompt: Where has contentment felt difficult this week? What would it look like to choose gratitude over scarcity in that place?
day3.practice: Name one area where gratitude is replacing scarcity today.

sharedEncouragement3day.title: 3-Day Shared Encouragement Practice
sharedEncouragement3day.description: Three days of mutual encouragement — notice one another, sharpen one another, and build each other up in a small shared circle.

day1.principle: Let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together.
day1.prompt: Write one person you want to encourage today and one reason they matter.
day1.practice: Name one concrete encouragement for a friend.

day2.principle: Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another.
day2.prompt: Share one insight or observation from your day that might help someone else grow.
day2.practice: Offer one honest, sharpening observation with kindness.

day3.principle: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom.
day3.prompt: What has changed in you this week because someone else walked with you?
day3.practice: Thank someone for the way they have helped you keep going.

waiting5day.title: 5-Day Waiting Practice
waiting5day.description: Five days of holding a decision steady — naming the urgency, finding the fear beneath it, and waiting for wisdom to settle.

day1.principle: Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the Lord.
day1.prompt: Name the decision or pressure you are carrying. Write one line describing what urgency is asking you to do.
day1.practice: Name the decision and what urgency is whispering.

day2.principle: Let your eyes look directly forward, and your gaze be straight before you. Ponder the path of your feet; then all your ways will be sure.
day2.prompt: What would it cost to wait three more days before deciding? Write the real fear beneath the urgency.
day2.practice: Name the fear beneath the urgency.

day3.principle: They who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles.
day3.prompt: What is one sign that waiting has been good so far — even something small?
day3.practice: Write one sign that waiting is protecting something good.

day4.principle: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him.
day4.prompt: Have you asked a trusted voice about this decision? Write what you have heard or what you would ask them.
day4.practice: Write what counsel has said — or what you would ask.

day5.principle: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.
day5.prompt: After five days, what has changed in how you see this decision? What is the next faithful step — even if it is another week of waiting?
day5.practice: Name the next faithful step with an open hand.

stewardship7day.title: 7-Day Stewardship Practice
stewardship7day.description: Seven days of honest accounting — what you have been given, where haste is shaping choices, and what enough looks like right now.

day1.principle: Remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth.
day1.prompt: Write one way your income or resources have come to you — something you did not fully earn on your own.
day1.practice: Acknowledge one resource that was given, not only earned.

day2.principle: The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty.
day2.prompt: Where are you making a financial decision in haste? Name it and write what slow discernment would ask.
day2.practice: Name one area where haste is shaping spending.

day3.principle: One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
day3.prompt: What is one small area of financial faithfulness you have practised recently? Write it down as an act of gratitude, not pride.
day3.practice: Name one small area where faithfulness has shown up.

day4.principle: Owe no one anything, except to love each other.
day4.prompt: Look at your debts — student, personal, consumer, or relational. Write one honest sentence about what you owe and what faithful next step looks like.
day4.practice: Write one honest sentence about what you owe.

day5.principle: Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
day5.prompt: Write about the last time you gave freely — without guilt or pressure. What made it joyful?
day5.practice: Name one act of giving that came from freedom, not compulsion.

day6.principle: You cannot serve God and money.
day6.prompt: Where is money making a decision that should belong to wisdom, relationships, or rest? Name it without shame.
day6.practice: Name one place where money is leading instead of serving.

day7.principle: Godliness with contentment is great gain.
day7.prompt: After seven days, write what is enough for this season. Not an ideal — what is actually enough right now?
day7.practice: Write what is enough for this season, plainly.

sabbathRest5day.title: 5-Day Sabbath Rest Practice
sabbathRest5day.description: Five days of protected rest, naming the work rhythm, the strain beneath it, and making space to slow down.

day1.principle: Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
day1.prompt: Name the work rhythm you are carrying. Write one line about what keeps rest from feeling easy.
day1.practice: Name the rhythm and what makes rest feel hard.

day2.principle: The Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath.
day2.prompt: What would it look like to let rest serve you instead of making rest another task?
day2.practice: Write one way rest could serve you today.

day3.principle: Be still, and know that I am God.
day3.prompt: What noise, pace, or demand needs to quiet down first?
day3.practice: Name one thing to let grow still.

day4.principle: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.
day4.prompt: Where is your attention scattered between many things? Write the single need that matters most.
day4.practice: Name the one thing that needs your attention most.

day5.principle: If you call the Sabbath a delight ... then you shall take delight in the Lord.
day5.prompt: What would make rest feel like delight rather than duty this week?
day5.practice: Choose one small delight that restores you.

listening3day.title: Listening Practice
listening3day.description: Three days to slow down, listen first, and hear what lies beneath the first answer.

day1.principle: Let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
day1.prompt: Who or what needs your first full attention today?

day2.principle: If one gives an answer before he hears, it is his folly and shame.
day2.prompt: What question are you rushing past?

day3.principle: The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
day3.prompt: Where would a better question help more than a quick opinion?

repair4day.title: Repair Practice
repair4day.description: Four days to name hurt honestly, lower defensiveness, and move toward repair.

day1.principle: First be reconciled to your brother.
day1.prompt: Who needs your attention because something is unresolved?
day1.practice: Name the relationship that needs repair.

day2.principle: Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger.
day2.prompt: Where has anger been left to simmer?
day2.practice: Take one step before the sun sets.

day3.principle: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another.
day3.prompt: What confession or apology would make the next conversation more honest?
day3.practice: Write the apology you have been avoiding.

day4.principle: If possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all.
day4.prompt: What is the most faithful peace you can pursue without pretending everything is fine?
day4.practice: Choose peace as far as it depends on you.

generosity7day.title: Generosity Practice
generosity7day.description: Seven days of giving from conviction, not pressure, while honoring capacity and wise limits.

day1.principle: A generous person will be enriched, and one who waters will himself be watered.
day1.prompt: Where have you received more than you notice?
day1.practice: Notice one place abundance wants to move.

day2.principle: It is acceptable according to what a person has, not according to what he does not have.
day2.prompt: What is a generous amount for this season, not an ideal season?
day2.practice: Name a proportion that fits your capacity.

day3.principle: It is more blessed to give than to receive.
day3.prompt: Who could be strengthened by what is already in your hand?

day4.principle: Whoever is generous to the poor lends to the Lord.
day4.prompt: What act of mercy would you like to remember instead of fear?
day4.practice: Write one way kindness can be practical.

day5.principle: Set your hope on God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy.
day5.prompt: What does hope look like when riches are not the center?
day5.practice: Set your hope on something sturdier than money.

day6.principle: You will be enriched in every way to be generous in every way.
day6.prompt: Where does gratitude make giving feel freer?
day6.practice: Give thanks for what you can share.

day7.principle: Because of this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in all that you undertake.
day7.prompt: What gift feels cheerful and sustainable right now?
day7.practice: Choose the next generous step with joy.

attentionFast5day.title: Attention Fast
attentionFast5day.description: Five days to clear noise, recover focus, and choose what deserves attention.

day1.principle: Teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom.
day1.prompt: Where is your time leaking away?

day2.principle: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
day2.prompt: What is shaping your inner life without permission?

day3.principle: The eye is the lamp of the body.
day3.prompt: What brings clarity, and what clouds it?
day3.practice: Let your attention rest on one clear thing.

day4.principle: Be transformed by the renewal of your mind.
day4.prompt: What pattern is normal but not wise?

day5.principle: Whatever is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, and commendable, think about these things.
day5.prompt: What is true, honorable, and worth keeping in view?
day5.practice: Name one thing worth your attention.

hiddenService5day.title: Hidden Service
hiddenService5day.description: Five days to serve quietly, release credit, and notice faithfulness no one needs to see.

day1.principle: Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
day1.prompt: Where can you do good without announcing it?
day1.practice: Choose one hidden act of service.

day2.prompt: How can freedom become loving action instead of self-focus?
day2.practice: Serve in a way no one needs to praise.

day3.principle: As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another.
day3.prompt: What gift can you use to help someone else today?
day3.practice: Use one gift to bless another.

day4.principle: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.
day4.prompt: What changes when you serve for God rather than applause?

day5.principle: God is not unjust so as to overlook your work and the love you have shown.
day5.prompt: Who has been quietly helped by your consistency?
day5.practice: Notice the good that has already been done.

readWithMe7day.title: Reading Practice
readWithMe7day.description: Seven days of reading attentively, asking what is true, and letting wisdom shape your hearing.

day1.principle: An intelligent heart acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
day1.prompt: What do you want to understand more deeply?
day1.practice: Read one passage with fuller attention.

day2.principle: Let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
day2.prompt: What would it look like to be quick to hear and slow to speak?

day3.principle: The beginning of wisdom is this: Get wisdom.
day3.prompt: Where do you need wisdom more than more information?

day4.principle: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
day4.prompt: What is the lamp for the next step, not the whole map?
day4.practice: Let one line guide your next step.

day5.principle: They received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily.
day5.prompt: What would it mean to test what you hear with care?

day6.principle: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.
day6.prompt: What word needs to dwell richly in you today?
day6.practice: Sit with one passage longer than usual.

day7.principle: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, rightly handling the word of truth.
day7.prompt: What does faithful handling of truth look like now?
day7.practice: Read with care, patience, and humility.
